analysis: The only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1751) is a documentation row adding the env var DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP to the daemon-forwarded environment table. The row points to ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey). Per the row, `0` disables the load-time shape warmup and `always` skips its shader-cache probe. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption or coordinator protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The supplied base excerpts (lines 1-830) do not include the changed region and only provide surrounding context. Threat-model relevance: T-041 (prefix-cache TTFT timing oracle, SEC-035) and TB-007. A load-time warmup that changes TTFT shape could in principle affect timing characteristics, but nothing visible shows it touching the prefix cache, cacheSalt scoping, HMAC lookup tags, TTL or the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate. The warmup uses a synthetic shape, and the threat model does not claim it as a control. The implementing Swift source (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift) was not supplied. Whether the warmup uses real consumer prompt data, or how the forwarded env var is validated or interacts with launchd passthrough, is unverified. Because the PR touches documentation only, this is a coverage limit rather than a finding. No regression or new attack surface is identified from the supplied evidence. A reviewer of the accompanying Swift change should confirm that the warmup uses only synthetic tokens, does not populate the SSD prefix cache with any scope that could collide with real account scopes, and does not retain residual GPU/KV data (T-028).
